mainTopic: פנחס's descent from יוסף and יתרו, checking a bride's brothers, the story of יהונתן the priest of מיכה's idol and his later תשובה, and the source that sons inherit their father before daughters
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining how פנחס came from both יוסף and יתרו. One of his mother's parents came from each family, and the plural wording 'daughters of פוטיאל' supports this. רבא then learns from the extra words 'sister of נחשון' that a man should check a woman's brothers before marrying her, because most sons take after their mother's brothers. Next the גמרא tells the story of יהונתן, a descendant of משה who served as a priest for מיכה's idol. The men of דן rebuke him with words that echo פסוקים about משה. He answers with a family saying that it is better to work even for עבודה זרה than to depend on others. The גמרא says he misread that saying: it really meant humble work that feels beneath you, as רב told רב כהנא. Later דוד put יהונתן over the treasuries, and the פסוק calls him שבואל because he returned to God with all his heart. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה and asks for the source that sons inherit their father ahead of daughters. רב פפא challenges the proof, and אביי begins a reply that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: פנחס's mother came from both families
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the question by saying that one of פנחס's mother's parents came from יוסף and the other came from יתרו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the answer is this: if his mother's father came from יוסף, then his mother's mother came from יתרו. And if his mother's father came from יתרו, then his mother's mother came from יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer to how פנחס can be a descendant of both יוסף and יתרו: his mother's two parents came from the two different families.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that earlier suggestions are set aside. The new answer splits the two family lines between his mother's father and his mother's mother. This way both claims are true at once.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a new answer that replaces earlier ones

phrases.english: Rather: if his mother's father was from Yosef,
phrases.notes: 'His' means פנחס, the person the גמרא has been talking about.

phrases.english: his mother's mother was from Yisro;
if his mother's father was from Yisro,
his mother's mother was from Yosef.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question from the earlier part of the daf about how פנחס is descended from both יוסף and יתרו.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the family lines: one maternal grandparent from each family
steps.terutzHavaAmina: That פנחס came from only one of them, or that the two claims contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: His mother's two parents came one from יוסף and one from יתרו, so both claims are true

steps.title: The plural wording of the פסוק supports this
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'from the daughters of פוטיאל' in the plural, which shows that פנחס came from two people called פוטי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording of the פסוק is also exact, since it says 'from the daughters of פוטיאל'. Learn from this that there were two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer from the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said 'daughter of פוטיאל'. The plural 'daughters' hints at two family lines, both connected to the name פוטי, namely יוסף and יתרו. This matches the answer just given.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact; a support taken from precise wording
A name in the פסוק understood as hinting at both יוסף and יתרו

steps.whatToRemember: פנחס came from both יוסף and יתרו through his mother's two parents, and the plural 'daughters of פוטיאל' hints at this.

phrases.english: It is also precise, as it is written:
"from the daughters of Putiel"
phrases.notes: שמות 6:25. Notice the plural 'daughters'. That is the hint the גמרא is pointing to.

phrases.english: learn from it: two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from the פסוק for the answer in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That פנחס descended from two family lines, יוסף and יתרו
steps.raayaSupportSource: The plural wording 'מבנות פוטיאל' in שמות 6:25

steps.title: Check a woman's brothers before marrying her
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that a man marrying a woman should check what her brothers are like. He learns this from the extra words 'sister of נחשון'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: a man who marries a woman should check her brothers. As it says: 'אהרן took אלישבע, daughter of עמינדב, sister of נחשון.' Once it says 'daughter of עמינדב', don't I already know she is נחשון's sister? Why does the פסוק add 'sister of נחשון'? From here we learn that a man marrying a woman should check her brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new teaching and proves it from an extra phrase in the פסוק about אהרן's marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחשון was the son of עמינדב, so 'daughter of עמינדב' already tells us she was his sister. Since the Torah adds 'sister of נחשון' anyway, רבא reads it as a lesson that her brothers matter when choosing a wife. This teaching connects to the previous discussion of family lines.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs to check her brothers
From the meaning of what is already stated
Why does the פסוק need to say this?

phrases.english: Rava said: One who marries a woman
needs to examine her brothers,
as it is said: "And Aaron took Elisheva,
daughter of Amminadav, sister of Nachshon"
from what is implied when it says "daughter of Amminadav,"
do I not know that she is Nachshon's sister?
phrases.notes: נחשון was עמינדב's son, so any daughter of עמינדב is automatically his sister.

phrases.english: Why does the verse say "sister of Nachshon"?
From here: one who marries a woman
needs to examine her brothers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַנּוֹשֵׂא אִשָּׁה, צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּבְדּוֹק בְּאַחֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching that continues the theme of family background, which was the subject of steps 1 and 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who marries a woman should first check what her brothers are like.

steps.title: Why the brothers matter
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains רבא's rule: most sons take after their mother's brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: most sons resemble their mother's brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the reason behind רבא's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said to check the brothers but did not say why. The ברייתא explains that a man's future sons are likely to resemble her brothers. So checking her brothers is a way of seeing what his children may be like.
steps.whatToRemember: Check a woman's brothers before marrying her, because most sons take after their mother's brothers.

phrases.english: It was taught: Most sons
resemble the mother's brothers.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: רוֹב בָּנִים דּוֹמִין לַאֲחֵי הָאֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבא's rule in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that one should check a woman's brothers
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: most sons resemble the mother's brothers

steps.title: The פסוק about the visit of שבט דן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק in which the men of שבט דן find יהונתן serving at מיכה's house and ask him three questions.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They turned aside there and said to him: Who brought you here, what are you doing in this place, and what do you have here?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about יהונתן, the priest of מיכה's idol. It is setting up the next step, which will explain why the פסוק uses three separate questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three questions seem to repeat each other. The words 'here' (הלם), 'what' (מה) and 'here' (פה) will each be connected to a different פסוק about משה in the next step.

phrases.english: "And they turned aside there, and said:
phrases.notes: שופטים 18:3. The men of דן are speaking to יהונתן, who was serving at מיכה's idol.

phrases.english: Who brought you here,
and what are you doing in this place,
and what do you have here?"

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיָּסוּרוּ שָׁמָּה, וַיֹּאמֶר: מִי הֱבִיאֲךָ הֲלֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new topic: the story of יהונתן, who was mentioned earlier in the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The base פסוק: the men of דן ask יהונתן three questions.

steps.title: Aren't you a descendant of משה?
steps.stepSummary: Each of the three questions is read as a reminder that יהונתן comes from משה. The point is: how can you serve as a priest for an idol?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Don't you come from משה, about whom it says 'Do not come close here'? Don't you come from משה, about whom it says 'What is that in your hand'? Don't you come from משה, about whom it says 'And you, stand here with me'? And you will become a priest for עבודה זרה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains each question by matching one word to a פסוק about משה. Together the questions become a harsh rebuke of יהונתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלם, מה and פה each recall a פסוק about משה. This shows the men were really saying: 'You come from משה, so how can you do this?' The questions are a challenge to his behavior, not requests for information.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest who serves an idol

steps.confusionAlert: These questions are not real requests for information. Each one is a hint to a פסוק about משה, and together they rebuke יהונתן.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לָאו מִמֹּשֶׁה קָא אָתֵית,
phrases.english: They said to him: Do you not come from Moshe,
about whom it is written: "Do not draw close here"?
Do you not come from Moshe,
about whom it is written: "What is that in your hand"?
Do you not come from Moshe,
about whom it is written: "And you, stand here with me"?
Shall you become a priest for idol worship?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לָאו מִמֹּשֶׁה קָא אָתֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the three questions of the פסוק quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: יהונתן's decision to serve as a priest for idol worship
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A descendant of משה, who stood close to ה׳, should never serve an idol.

steps.title: יהונתן's family tradition
steps.stepSummary: יהונתן answers that he has a family tradition: it is better to hire yourself out even to עבודה זרה than to depend on other people.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This is what I received from the house of my father's father: a person should always hire himself out to עבודה זרה rather than need other people.
steps.whatsHappening: יהונתן defends himself against the rebuke by quoting a teaching passed down in his family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He says that depending on charity is so bad that taking a job even at an idol's temple is better. He presents his job as a way to support himself, not as real belief in the idol.

keyTerms.meaning: I have received as a tradition
A person should hire himself out
Need other people (depend on their help)

steps.whatToRemember: The men of דן rebuked יהונתן for serving an idol even though he came from משה. He answered with a family tradition that working, even at a job like that, is better than depending on others.
steps.confusionAlert: יהונתן is not presented as believing in the idol. He explains that he took the job so he would not have to live off other people.

phrases.english: He said to them: Thus I have received
from the house of my father's father:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם יַשְׂכִּיר אָדָם עַצְמוֹ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: A person should always hire himself out to idol worship
and not need other people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן, כָּךְ מְקוּבְּלַנִי מִבֵּית אֲבִי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: יהונתן responds to the rebuke in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can a descendant of משה serve as a priest for an idol?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A family tradition says it is better to hire oneself out even to עבודה זרה than to depend on other people.

steps.title: יהונתן misread his family saying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says יהונתן took 'עבודה זרה' literally, but the saying really meant work that feels foreign or beneath you.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהונתן thought the saying meant real idol worship. That is not true. 'עבודה זרה' here means work that is strange to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps in and says יהונתן's answer in step 7 came from a wrong reading of his family saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying was 'hire yourself out even to עבודה זרה rather than depend on others.' יהונתן read it as actual idol service. The גמרא reads the words as 'עבודה שזרה לו', work that feels foreign to a person's dignity. So the lesson is about doing humble work, not about serving idols.

keyTerms.meaning: and he thought (but he was wrong)
work that is strange (unfitting) to him

steps.confusionAlert: The family tradition never allowed idol worship. The mistake was יהונתן's reading of it, not the tradition itself.

phrases.english: And he thought it meant actual idol worship;
but that is not so,
rather, 'strange service' means
work that is strange to him,
phrases.notes: A play on words: 'strange work' here means work that feels foreign or beneath a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהוּא סָבַר – לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מַמָּשׁ; וְלָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects how יהונתן understood the saying he quoted in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: יהונתן's literal reading of 'עבודה זרה' in his family saying
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He took 'עבודה זרה' as idol worship when it meant humbling labor.

steps.title: רב's advice to רב כהנא shows the real meaning
steps.stepSummary: רב told רב כהנא to do even messy, lowly work for pay rather than say it is beneath him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב said to רב כהנא: skin a dead animal in the market and take your wages. Do not say, 'I am a great man, and this is beneath me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its reading with a real teaching from רב to his student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Skinning a dead animal in public was dirty, low-status work. רב says even an important person should do it rather than depend on others. This is the same idea as 'work that is strange to him.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a lasting lesson that honest work, even lowly work, is better than depending on others.

phrases.english: as Rav said to Rav Kahana:
Skin a carcass in the market
and take payment,
and do not say:
I am a great man
and this matter is beneath me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading given in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The reading 'עבודה שזרה לו' means humble work

steps.title: דוד puts יהונתן in charge of the treasuries
steps.stepSummary: דוד saw that יהונתן loved money very much, so he made him head of the treasuries, as the פסוק about שבואל shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: When דוד saw that money was very dear to him, he appointed him over the treasuries, as it says: 'And שבואל son of גרשום son of מנשה was ruler over the treasuries.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues יהונתן's story and tells what happened to him later in life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because יהונתן cared so much about money, דוד gave him a job looking after money. The proof is a פסוק that names the treasury head as a descendant of גרשום, and the גמרא takes this to be יהונתן.

phrases.english: When David saw
that money was very precious to him,
he appointed him over the treasuries,
as it is said:
'And Shevuel son of Gershom son of Menashe
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 26:24. The פסוק itself says בן משה, and some versions here say משה too.

phrases.english: was ruler over the treasuries.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁרָאָה דָּוִד שֶׁמָּמוֹן חָבִיב עָלָיו בְּיוֹתֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the יהונתן story after the correction in steps 8-9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד appointed יהונתן over the treasuries because he loved money.

steps.title: But his name was יהונתן, not שבואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק can call him שבואל when his name was יהונתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was his name שבואל? His name was יהונתן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem: the פסוק uses a different name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the treasury officer is יהונתן, why does the פסוק call him שבואל? This seems to undo the claim that the פסוק is about him.

keyTerms.meaning: and is it really so that...?

phrases.english: And was his name Shevuel?
Wasn't his name Jonathan!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי שְׁבוּאֵל שְׁמוֹ? וַהֲלֹא יְהוֹנָתָן שְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the identification made in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the שבואל of the פסוק as יהונתן

steps.title: שבואל means he returned to God
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the name שבואל shows that he returned to God with all his heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: he is called this because he returned to God with all his heart.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that שבואל is a name describing what יהונתן became.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבואל sounds like 'שב לאל', returned to God. So the פסוק uses a new name to show that יהונתן did תשובה. This answers the question and gives the story a good ending.
steps.whatToRemember: יהונתן's story ends with תשובה: the man who served an idol later returned fully to God and was trusted over the treasuries.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
that he returned to God with all his heart.
phrases.notes: שְׁבוּ-אֵל is read as שָׁב לָאֵל, 'returned to God.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שֶׁשָּׁב לָאֵל בְּכׇל לִבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the name question from step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the name as a description
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שבואל must be a different person from יהונתן.
steps.terutzMaskana: שבואל is יהונתן, renamed for his complete תשובה.

steps.title: Where do we learn that sons inherit their father?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks for the source that sons inherit their father.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: and sons inherit the father. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The story is finished, and the גמרא now returns to the list of inheritors in the משנה and asks for a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed sons as heirs of their father. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches that sons inherit, and that they come before daughters.

phrases.english: And sons inherit the father.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the list of inheritors in the משנה.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that sons inherit their father ahead of daughters

steps.title: The verse gives the daughter the inheritance only when there is no son
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says a daughter inherits when there is no son, so when there is a son, the son comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'If a man dies [and has no son]...' The daughter inherits only because there is no son. If there is a son, the son comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק and draws a conclusion from what it says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה gives the inheritance to the daughter 'if he has no son.' The גמרא reads this to mean that a son, when there is one, takes precedence over a daughter.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'If a man dies, etc.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:8. It continues: 'and has no son, pass his inheritance to his daughter.'

phrases.english: The reason is that he has no son,

phrases.aramaic: הָא יֵשׁ לוֹ בֵּן – בֵּן קוֹדֵם.
phrases.english: but if he has a son, the son comes first.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'and has no son' in במדבר 27:8 imply that a son takes precedence over a daughter.

steps.title: רב פפא: maybe neither inherits when there is a son and a daughter
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the פסוק might only cover a son alone or a daughter alone, so maybe when both exist, neither inherits.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Say instead: if there is a son, the son inherits. If there is a daughter, the daughter inherits. If there is a son and a daughter, neither one inherits!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks the proof by offering a different way to read the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק clearly teaches that a daughter inherits when she is alone. But רב פפא asks: how do we know that 'the son comes first' when both a son and a daughter are present? On his reading, the פסוק says nothing about that case. It is a strange possibility, raised to show that the proof is not airtight.
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not ruling that nobody inherits. He is testing whether the פסוק really proves that the son comes first.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי, אֵימָא:
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye: Say instead:
if there is a son, let the son inherit;
if there is a daughter, let the daughter inherit;
if there is a son and a daughter,

phrases.aramaic: לָא הַאי לֵירוֹת וְלָא הַאי לֵירוֹת!
phrases.english: neither this one should inherit nor that one!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי, אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference drawn in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference 'הא יש לו בן – בן קודם'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק may only cover cases where one child is alone, leaving the son-and-daughter case unresolved.

steps.title: אביי begins his reply
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts answering רב פפא with 'ואלא', and his reply continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: This word only sets up the next move: אביי is starting to push back against רב פפא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ואלא' usually opens a pushback: 'if not my way, then what?' The full content of אביי's answer comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: And rather,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins אביי's response to רב פפא's challenge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not yet given; אביי's defense of the inference continues on the next amud.
